samples.summary: `nodeAt` indexes an array with an unvalidated, client-controlled path element, reaching `Array.prototype` members and then crashing the process
samples.evidence: `anchor.path` originates from the browser client (`POST /__design-editor/mutate` per docs/design/design-editor/design-editor-engine.md:131-141) and is documented as `number[]` but never validated at runtime. JSON permits strings, so a path of `["constructor"]` makes `kids[i]` resolve to `Array.prototype.constructor` — truthy, so the `if (!kids[i]) return null` guard at line 794 passes. `node` then becomes `undefined` (`.node` of the Array constructor) and the function returns `undefined`, violating its documented `JsxRootNode | null` contract. With a two-element path such as `["constructor","0"]` the next iteration calls `childrenOf(undefined, undefined)`, where `ts.isJsxElement(undefined)` dereferences `.kind` and throws an uncaught TypeError — an unhandled exception inside the dev-server middleware. The tests only cover `[9]`, `[0,0,0]` and `[-1]` (test/server/jsx-nodes.test.mjs:349-356); no non-numeric key is exercised. Fix: coerce/validate each index with `Number.isInteger(i) && i >= 0` before indexing.

samples.summary: Client-supplied `component`/`tag`/`fp` are reflected verbatim (inside angle brackets) into `reason` strings returned across the trust boundary
samples.evidence: `resolveNode` echoes untrusted anchor fields straight into the returned `reason`: line 685 (`...named ${anchor.component}`), line 690, and lines 712-713 which wrap client input in literal angle brackets (`<${anchor.tag}>`) alongside `anchor.fp` and `anchor.path`. These strings are designed to be surfaced in the sandbox UI ("the reason carries the candidate paths so the UI can offer 're-point this edit'", line 664). If the client renders `reason` with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` or into a template, an anchor with `tag: "img src=x onerror=…"` yields stored/reflected script in the editor UI. I could not confirm the sink: no client renderer exists in this repo yet (no `src/sandbox/` in packages/design-editor). Hardening: escape or omit raw anchor echoes, or return structured fields rather than a prose string.

samples.summary: 32-bit truncated SHA-1 is the only integrity check that a write lands on the intended node
samples.evidence: `fpOf` (line 614) and `fpxOf` (line 644) truncate SHA-1 to 8 hex chars — 32 bits. That digest is the sole verification that the `path` hint still points at the anchored node (`at.fp === anchor.fp`, line 697) and the sole key for the relocation searches (lines 703-704). A truncated 32-bit digest is trivially collidable by construction: anyone who can influence the source file (a dependency-supplied component, a co-contributor, or the agent that generates JSX) can craft a node whose fp equals another node's, defeating the 'exactly one match' safety property and steering a write onto the wrong node — precisely the silent wrong-node failure the module is built to prevent. Accidental collisions in a large file are also non-negligible at 32 bits. Fix: keep the full digest, or at minimum 16 hex chars (64 bits); SHA-1 itself is also a poor default even for non-security digests.

samples.summary: The structural-edit guard is opt-in (`opts.requireStatic` defaults to false), so it is bypassed by any caller that simply omits the flag
samples.evidence: `resolveNode(sf, anchor, opts = {})` at line 677 enforces the scope / owner / top-level-return guards only inside `if (opts.requireStatic)` (line 725). The doc comment asserts the guard 'lives HERE, server-side, rather than as a disabled button, because the client's SceneMeta can be stale' (lines 667-669) — but a default-off parameter is not an enforced path: a future `inject.mjs` op that forgets the flag receives a fully resolved node with no scope check and can splice inside an `iteration` scope or into a `{…}` container, corrupting the consumer's source file. Nothing in the repo enforces the flag: grep shows `requireStatic` appears only in this file and its test. Safer shape: default to enforcing and require an explicit opt-out per op, or split into `resolveNodeForStructural` / `resolveNodeForProps`. Reported as an unenforceable-by-default guard rather than a live bypass because no production call site exists yet.

samples.summary: No input validation at the module's designated trust boundary: `anchor` is consumed as trusted-shaped JSON
samples.evidence: `resolveNode` is documented as the server-side resolver for anchors that arrive from the browser over the unauthenticated dev-server endpoints (`/mutate`, `/validate`, `/candidates` — docs/design/design-editor/design-editor-engine.md:1321-1347). It performs no type/shape validation on `anchor.component` (used as a map key), `anchor.path` (array-indexed, see the `nodeAt` finding), `anchor.tag`, `anchor.fp` or `anchor.fpx`. The prototype hazard on `roots` is correctly handled by `Object.create(null)` (line 443) and covered by tests, which shows the author was aware of the untrusted-key problem — but the same untrusted values reach array indexing and string interpolation unchecked. Since the HTTP host (`vite.config.ts` mutationBridge) does not exist in this repo yet, this module is currently the only place such validation could live. Add a schema/shape check (component is a string, path is an array of non-negative integers, fp/fpx match /^[0-9a-f]{8}$/) at the entry point.

samples.summary: Unbounded recursion over attacker-influenced source ASTs can exhaust the stack and kill the dev-server process
samples.evidence: `pushExpr` recurses on `BinaryExpression` left/right (lines 359-363), `walkNode` recurses per depth level (line 561), and `findJsxRoots`' `visit` walks the entire file recursively (line 505). None carry a depth cap. A source file with a long left-nested `a && b && c && …` chain or deeply nested JSX (generated code, a vendored/minified component, or a file produced by the agent the editor drives) overflows the stack and throws a RangeError that no caller catches, terminating the request handler and — if the dev-server middleware does not trap it — the Node process. Additionally `resolveNode` re-runs `findJsxRoots` plus a full walk on every call (lines 678, 692), so a client with access to the unauthenticated dev endpoint can amplify CPU per request. Dev-only impact, hence minor.

samples.summary: `identity` is built on a plain `{}` while `roots` is hardened with `Object.create(null)` — inconsistent, and it is read back by key in `fpOf`
samples.evidence: `attrsOf` creates `const identity = {}` (line 180) keyed by JSX attribute names, and `fpOf` reads `identity[a] ?? ''` for each allowlisted name (line 606). Not exploitable today because writes are gated on `IDENTITY_ATTRS.includes(name)` (line 195) and none of those names (`to, href, id, name, htmlFor, type, value, data-testid, aria-label, role, key`) exist on `Object.prototype` — but the object is also part of the exported `fpOf` signature, so a caller passing a JSON-parsed `identity` (e.g. rehydrated `SceneNodeMeta.identity` from `design-metadata.json`) inherits whatever `Object.prototype` carries, silently changing a fingerprint. Use `Object.create(null)` here too, matching the deliberate hardening at line 443.
